title: OpenAI updates ChatGPT with interactive graphics
key_facts: OpenAI announced Intelligent UI, a ChatGPT feature that creates interactive visual interfaces, in its announcement on Wednesday (14 Oct 2026).
OpenAI says GPT-6 was trained to compose responses from text, visuals and interactive elements such as graphics, tappable buttons, forms and charts.
Examples: an interactive diagram of a bicycle, a graph to explain GDP, a calculator to split a bill, a retirement-savings projection.
ChatGPT still gives text-only answers when that is the most suitable format.
OpenAI built a component library the model draws from when building interactive content.
Available to Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users from Wednesday and to Free and Go users from Thursday as they move to GPT-6.
GPT-6 launched for paid ChatGPT in September, replacing GPT-5.6; that rollout did not include Intelligent UI.
quote_evidence: "We’ve trained GPT‑6 to compose responses using text, visuals and interactive elements, choosing how they fit together based on your question," OpenAI wrote in its announcement on Wednesday.
The AI chatbot will still provide text-only responses when that is the most suitable format to respond to input.

This feature will now be available to users on ChatGPT's Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise tiers from Wednesday, subsequently rolling out to Free and Go tiers from Thursday as they also transition to GPT-6.
why_it_matters_hint: ChatGPT answers can now be interactive tools rather than just text, across all plans.
notes: Disclosure in Mashable's article: Ziff Davis sued OpenAI in April 2025 over copyright.
